title: Security settings
purpose: See the laboratory's security and privacy contacts, set the session limits, who must have a second sign-in factor and whether staff confirm it is them before revealing patient information, and see what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information here, with who sets each part.
summary: Your security and privacy contacts, the session limits and sign-in rules you set, and what protects sign-in, sessions and patient information here. Only the admin role can open this page.

tasks.title: Record or change a contact
steps: Under Security and privacy contacts select [[Security contact]] or [[Privacy contact]].
Enter the name or office and any title, email and phone, explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Change when sessions are signed out
steps: Under Session limits select [[Staff]] or [[Client portal]].
Set [[Sign out after no activity for]] (5 to 60 minutes) and [[Longest session]] (1 to 24 hours), explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Require a second sign-in factor
steps: Tick the accounts that must have one, explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]]. It applies at each account's next sign-in.

tasks.title: Ask staff to confirm before revealing patient information
steps: Tick [[Confirm it is you before the first reveal in a session]], explain why in [[Reason]] and select [[Save changes]].

tasks.title: Find out who sets a protection
steps: Find the setting in its group (Sign-in, Sessions, Patient information or Connection) and read [[Set by]].
A deployment setting names its environment variable. Ask whoever runs the deployment to change it.

good_to_know: You change the contacts, the session limits, the second-factor rule and the confirmation before revealing here, each with a reason; all but the contacts ask you to confirm it is you.
A shorter limit applies from each session's next request: a session already idle longer is signed out then.
A second-factor rule applies at each account's next sign-in; sessions it did not cover at sign-in are not interrupted.
Values are read from the running application each time the page opens. The page does not rate the deployment or say whether it meets any rule.
Staff see the contacts on the laboratory profile. Client portal accounts do not see them.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: Only the admin laboratory role can open this page, and the Setup menu lists it only for that role. Other staff roles, client portal accounts and a superuser without a laboratory role are refused. Every staff role reads the contacts on the laboratory profile instead.

sections.title: Security and privacy contacts
paragraphs: The person or office your laboratory names for questions about the security of its systems and the person or office it names for the privacy of patient information, as the laboratory records them. The application checks nothing against them and sends them nothing.

items.label: Contact
items.description: Security contact or Privacy contact. The name opens the contact's form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. It is plain text when the laboratory is not set up yet.

items.label: Name or office
items.description: The person or office. Not recorded when the contact has never been saved or was cleared.

items.label: Title or role, Email, Phone
items.description: As recorded, or a dash when blank. The email address opens your mail program.

sections.title: Session limits
paragraphs: After how long without activity a session is signed out, and how long a session may last at most, for staff accounts and for client portal accounts. Saving either audience's limits asks you to confirm it is you (your password, and a code if you have an authenticator app) unless you did in this browser in the last 5 minutes. Limits never saved show the starting values, 30 minutes and 12 hours. The server checks both on every request; a page warns 2 minutes before signing out for no activity, with Stay signed in, and 5 minutes before the longest session ends.

Opening a page, saving, searching or Stay signed in counts as activity. Reading or typing on a page does not. Signing in again returns to the page. When a limit signs a person out, what they were typing in a ticket's reply, note or logged contact, a new ticket logged by staff, a portal reply, a new portal ticket or a nonconformance form is kept for 24 hours, for them in that browser only, and comes back in that form when they sign in again (a nonconformance form's save is refused if the record changed since); typing in other forms is lost. The admin console does not warn before signing out.

items.label: Accounts
items.description: Staff or Client portal. The name opens that audience's form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. A portal account follows the Client portal limits and every other account the Staff limits, as the account is when each request arrives.

items.label: Sign out after no activity for
Longest session
items.description: Hours, from 1 to 24, counted from sign-in whatever the activity. Nothing extends it.

sections.title: Second sign-in factor
paragraphs: Which accounts the laboratory requires to have a second sign-in factor (an authenticator app, with recovery codes), as the rule stands when the page opens. Nothing is required until the rule is first saved. Edit opens the rule's form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. Saving it asks you to confirm it is you, as for the session limits.

Whether the rule covers an account is decided when it signs in. An account it covers without an authenticator app is sent to Set up a second sign-in factor after signing in and opens nothing else first. A session the rule did not cover at sign-in is not interrupted; a session it covered is sent to set one up whenever its account has none while the rule still covers it. Recovery codes alone do not count.

items.label: Accounts
items.description: Every staff account; Staff with these roles; Staff who can view patient information; Accounts that can open the admin console; Client portal accounts.

items.label: Second factor
items.description: Required (with the roles chosen, for the roles row) or Not required.

items.label: Active accounts required to have one
items.description: Under the table once the rule covers anyone: how many active accounts it covers now and how many of them have no authenticator app yet.

sections.title: Revealing patient information
paragraphs: Whether staff confirm it is them before the first reveal of patient information in each session, as the setting stands when the page opens. Nothing is asked until it is first saved. Edit opens its form; after saving or cancelling you return to this page. Saving it asks you to confirm it is you, as for the session limits.

When it is asked, the first Reveal of a patient-information value or Reveal key of a person-level link in a browser session sends the person to Confirm it is you (their password, and a code from their authenticator app or a recovery code where they have one) before anything is shown. Later reveals in that session are not asked. A confirmation they gave in that session in the last 5 minutes for another change counts; signing in does not. It is not asked before a search by a person-level key or for what client portal accounts see. Each reveal is recorded either way.

items.label: Confirm it is you before the first reveal in a session
items.description: Asked once in each session, or Not asked.

sections.title: Groups of settings
paragraphs: Sign-in: how accounts are created, the password rule (15 characters, or 8 for accounts the second-factor rule covers, which it names as the rule stands now), the second sign-in factor (Optional, or whom the rule above requires it of) with the number of active staff and client portal accounts that have one, what changing the second factor asks for, what Changing access and security settings asks for (the person's password, and their second factor where they have one, again before saving a change to an account or a role in the admin console, or to the session limits, the second-factor rule or the confirmation before revealing patient information here, unless they gave them in that browser in the last 5 minutes; ending an account's sessions does not ask), the limit on failed sign-ins (counted in the database, so every server process counts the same attempts), sign-in with an emailed code, where sign-ins are recorded, and the sign-in history the database keeps for each account (what it holds, that no entry can be changed or deleted, and that each person reads only their own).

Sessions: sign-out after a period without activity and the longest session (both from Session limits above), what closing the browser does, what deactivating an account and setting a new password do to its sessions, that each person sees where they are signed in and signs out the others (with where the recorded address comes from behind a proxy), that a superuser ends a person's sessions from the admin console with a reason, what marking a password as compromised does and who marks one, that the browser keeps no copy of the pages, and how the session cookie is sent.

Patient information: how many active staff accounts can view patient information, how many active ticket form fields are marked as holding patient information, Confirmation before a reveal (from Revealing patient information above: Asked once in each session or Not asked, with what it asks), how person-level links and the client portal show it, and where it is kept out of.
Connection: whether HTTPS is required and which content security policy is in force.

items.label: In force
items.description: The value the running application uses now, worked out when the page opens. Counts are of active accounts or active fields at that moment.

items.label: Set by
items.description: Where the value is changed. Session limits, above, Second sign-in factor, above, and Revealing patient information, above: you change it on this page. This release: behaviour written into the application, changed only by a new release. Application configuration: a value in the application's configuration: config/settings.py and config/logging.py in this release, or another settings module a deployment loads instead. Deployment setting: whoever runs the deployment changes it; the environment variable is named under it. Each person: every person decides for their own account. Accounts & roles: a superuser grants it in the administration. Ticket forms: the admin role marks fields on the ticket form setup pages. Not available yet: the application has no such setting.

items.label: Details
items.description: What the value means in practice, or a dash. Debug mode notes appear when the deployment runs in debug mode, which in this release's configuration turns off the HTTPS redirect and HTTPS-only session cookies. Changed in the application configuration means that what the value depends on differs from this release's, or could not be read: a setting, config/settings.py, config/logging.py or the settings module; the details name it, and the page describes the value no further.

items.label: History
items.description: The newest 20 changes to the security contact, the privacy contact, the session limits, the second sign-in factor rule and the confirmation before revealing patient information, shown oldest first: Lab contact changed, with the contact it changed and the name before and after; Lab session limits changed, with the accounts they apply to and each value before and after; Lab second factor rule changed, with whom it requires a second factor of and whom it did before; or Lab reveal confirmation changed, with whether the confirmation is asked once in each session or not asked, and what it was before; then the reason given, the time and the administrator who made it. The laboratory profile's history lists the contact changes too.
